open_questions.prompt: Acoustic tracking and inertial tracking are two methods used to determine a device's position. Compare these two types of tracking, focusing on how each method determines position and what environmental factors pose the greatest limitation for each.
open_questions.reference_answer: Acoustic tracking uses ultrasonic signals generated by stationary transmitters (speakers) to determine the real-time position of a moving receiver, but this requires the transmitter and receiver to be within the line of sight. Conversely, inertial trackers are self-contained sensors that measure changes in an object's motion, such as acceleration or orientation, using components like gyroscopes and accelerometers. Because inertial trackers are typically part of the device, they generally have no range limitations, but they only measure changes, not absolute values.

key_points.text: Acoustic tracking uses ultrasonic signals from stationary transmitters.
Acoustic tracking requires the transmitter and receiver to maintain line of sight.
Inertial trackers typically have no range limitation since they are part of the device.

open_questions.prompt: Advanced model-based techniques, such as SLAM and 3D structure sensing, are critical for modern AR. Explain how these two technologies fundamentally work to allow for stable and accurate real-time tracking in a real environment.
open_questions.reference_answer: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is a technique used to simultaneously create and update a map of the real environment while locating a position within that map, allowing for drift-free tracking. Parallel Tracking and Mapping (PTAM) is an optimization of SLAM designed specifically for augmented reality. In contrast, 3D structure sensing uses affordable commercial sensors to gather data on the 3D positions of points in the scene. This data is used to create high-quality 3D models of the environment's structures, which are then used for both tracking the system's pose and augmenting the real-world view.

key_points.text: SLAM simultaneously maps the environment while localizing the device within it.
3D structure sensing uses sensors to obtain 3D positions of points in a scene.
The 3D models created are used to track the sensor's pose and augment the view.
